Text: Goal: Nine games enter. After 31 days the colour with the most votes wins. Every face is a voter and every colour is a game. A big voter drags its followers along.
Click: Plug a voter for one Post. Click your own voter to reinforce it, or one with a closing ring to parry. Right-click your own voter to Rally. Hold SHIFT or press N for night shift. Space pauses.
Posts and gates: Posts are your energy and refill slowly. A famous voter is gated: it ignores you until enough of its followers back you. Win the edges first, then the hub.

Drift and attacks: Voters drift back to where their neighbours are, and a voter that shakes is about to flip. A ring in another game's colour announces an attack: click the voter to parry it, or Rally it.
Night shift: Sockpuppets ignore gates but add Heat and are fake votes. Heat above the red tick when the Mod Eye passes is a strike. Strikes never wear off and a final audit purges fake votes.
Winning: The front-runner draws everyone's attacks, so a lead has to be held. Your build sets your Posts and your first voters. Press H to read this again.
Nine games, one jam. After 31 days the colour with the most votes wins, and you are teal. Every face is a voter, every colour is a game, and the leaderboard counts how much each game's voters weigh.
Hover a voter to read it: who it backs, how sure it is, and whether you can flip it. Hover the voter in the spotlight.
Click the spotlit voter to Plug your game at it. Every Plug costs one Post (bottom left) and a weak voter flips in one.
The ring around a voter is its conviction. A strong voter takes several Plugs: each one drains the ring, and at zero it flips to you. Plug the spotlit voter until it flips.
Voters drift back to where their neighbours are. A voter that shakes is about to flip back, and the lines show who pushes it. Click it to reinforce it.
A padlock is a gate: a famous voter ignores you until enough of its followers already back you. Click the padlocked hub to see how far away you are.
Win the spotlit followers first. The gate ring fills as they come around, and once it opens the hub is a normal voter: flip it, and its followers follow.
Attacks are announced. A ring in the attacker's colour closes in on one of your voters, then plugs it. Click that voter to parry it for one Post before the ring lands.
Right-click a voter you hold to Rally it: one Post shields it and its neighbours from every plug for a few seconds. Try it on the spotlit voter.
That is the honest game: win the edges, open the gates, hold what you have. Night shift is the risky shortcut, and it has its own lesson.
Celebrities sit behind gates, and the honest way takes a long time. Click the spotlit celebrity to see its gate.
Hold SHIFT (or press N) for the night shift. The board goes dark and your clicks become sockpuppets that ignore gates. Holding it builds Heat (bottom bar).
Now click the celebrity. A sockpuppet flips it straight through the gate and adds {sockheat} Heat. Its visor marks it as a fake vote.
Fake votes keep you hot while you hold them, and a strike takes them all. Back it: plug your own sockpuppet until its ring is {launder} full and it turns into a real vote.
The Mod Eye sweeps every so often (top bar). If Heat is above the red tick when it passes, that is a strike. Let go of SHIFT and let Heat cool before it passes.

{strikes} strikes and you are out, and they never wear off. Once per jam you can Shift the Blame, but only for a small pile of fake votes. A final audit at the end purges every fake vote, so night shift is an opening move, not a last-second trick.
You know the whole game now. Pick a jam, spend your 12 hours on the build screen, and win it. The pop-up cards fill in the rest as it happens.
